0.long_answer: Cartilage‐hair hypoplasia is a syndromic form of primary immunodeficiency primarily characterized by a deficiency in T cells. This T-cell immunodeficiency manifests as abnormally low levels of lymphocytes in the blood, notably a reduction in PHA-responsive lymphocytes, which are essential for proper cell-mediated immune responses. Consequently, individuals with cartilage‐hair hypoplasia have a compromised immune system, particularly in their ability to fight infections that require robust T-cell function.
